violation_type.title: Required Equipment in Vehicles - List of Children (26 TAC §746.5617(a)(1))
violation_type.short_title: Required Equipment in Vehicles - List of Children
violation_type.typical_finding: This was evaluated during a DFPS investigation and found to be deficient.

finding_variants.text: This was evaluated during a DFPS investigation and found to be deficient.
The driver did not take the transportation binder which has the list of children's names with her during transport.

A caregiver did not have a list of the children for the van she was driving.   At school pick up, four children were put on her van, but she did not know which children they were and had no list to check or confirm.
The fire extinguishers in two vans which were using to transport children in care on 08/17/2022 were not secured in the passenger compartment. They were on the floor in passenger sides.

The following items are not being taken during transportation route:    -List of children being transported  -Emergency medical transport and treatment authorization forms for each child being transported  -Parent s names and telephone numbers and emergency telephone numbers for each child being transported
The operation did not have a list of children being transported to and from school.

occurrences.finding: Required Equipment in Vehicles - List of Children: The transportation driver did not utilize the list of children to conduct a name to face check to ensure all children were dropped off to their designated location.   Although, there was a list of children on the transportation vehicle, the driver did not follow the policy, which resulted in a child being dropped off at an incorrect location/school.
Required Equipment in Vehicles - List of Children: The list of children being transported was not available for review.     A child's name was missing from the list of children being transported.

Required Equipment in Vehicles - List of Children: During the investigation, interviews and other evidence collected determined that the operation was found deficient with this Minimum Standard. The evidence established that, although the parent notified the operation that the child required transportation from school, the child was not included on the transportation list and was not picked up as scheduled. As a result, the operation failed to maintain and utilize an accurate list of children to be transported, resulting in the child being left at school.
Required Equipment in Vehicles - List of Children: The list of children transported was not available for review.
